input.rationale: The only most-favoured-nation style covenant in the Agreement is Subparagraph 15.2, and it runs in our favour. It binds the "Terminal Parties" — identified in Subparagraph 4.1 as SingTel, TM, CWHKTI, China Telecom, KT, NTT Com, KDD and Chunghwa Telecom — to furnish transiting facilities on terms no less favorable than those granted to any other Carrier. Teleglobe USA Inc. is an Initial Party (p0053) but is not a Terminal Party, so we are a beneficiary of this MFN, not an obligor. That satisfies the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer; MFN in our favour is welcome), so no redline. Subparagraph 17.2 (p0225), the planner's candidate, only requires that Direct Access / Terminal Station arrangements negotiated by a Terminal Party be "reasonable and non-discriminatory" — an even-handed constraint on the Terminal Party, not a best-terms burden on us. Searches for "favourable/favorable", "no less", and most-favoured-nation phrasing surfaced no clause obliging us to extend any counterparty the benefit of better terms given to third parties.
